rpt_summary$env <- rownames(rpt_summary)
rpt_summary %<>%
  rename(lower = `lower.2.5%`, upper = `upper.97.5%`) %>%
  select(env, median, lower, upper) %>%
  mutate(env = as.factor(env))

## Merge them with the main dataframe for plotting 
R_cond.df_within %<>% left_join(rpt_summary, by = "env")



# Bind it all together ====

bbal_ker_condR_results <- rbind(condR_results, R_cond.df_between[,1:8], R_cond.df_within[,1:8])

save(bbal_ker_condR_results, file = "Data_outputs/bbal_ker_condR_results.RData")




# Make the plot ====
bathy_labels <- c("On shelf", "Near shelf break", "Off shelf")

condR_plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = R_cond.df_between, aes(x= env, y = median), col = col_between, size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(data = R_cond.df_between, aes(x = env, ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.1, colour = col_between) +
    geom_point(data = R_cond.df_within, aes(x= env, y = median), col = col_within, size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(data = R_cond.df_within, aes(x = env, ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.1, colour = col_within) +
    labs(y = "Conditional repeatability") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = bathy_labels) +
    expand_limits(y = c(0, 1)) +
    theme_bw() 

assign("bathy_condR_plot", condR_plot)




# [ 2 ] Plot individual slopes ---- 

rnd_effs.list <- list()

for (i in 1:2) {

  habitat_var = paste0(env_vars[i], "_scaled")
  
  # Get models
  load(paste0("Data_outputs/bbal_ker_glmm_within_", env_vars[i], ".RData"))
  load(paste0("Data_outputs/bbal_ker_glmm_between_", env_vars[i], ".RData"))

  mod_within = get(paste0("bbal_ker_glmm.within_", env_vars[i]))
  mod_between = get(paste0("bbal_ker_glmm.between_", env_vars[i]))
  
  # Get environmental range
  ind_ranges <- pnts_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    summarise(min_env = min(!!sym(habitat_var), na.rm = TRUE),
              max_env = max(!!sym(habitat_var), na.rm = TRUE)) 
  
  predictions.ind <- ind_ranges %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(habitat_val = list(seq(min_env, max_env, length.out = 100))) %>%
    rename(ring = ID) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(habitat_val)) 
  
  # Get random effects
  rnd_eff.within <- get_rnd_effects(mod_within, habitat_var) %>%
    separate(ID, c("ring", "season"), remove = F) %>% mutate(season_type = "Within season")
  rnd_eff.between <- get_rnd_effects(mod_between, habitat_var) %>%
    mutate(ring = ID, season = NA, season_type = "Between seasons")
  
  rnd_eff.all <- rbind(rnd_eff.within, rnd_eff.between) %>% mutate(env = env_vars[i])
  
  rnd_effs.list[[i]] <- rnd_eff.all
  
  predictions.ind <- merge(predictions.ind, rnd_eff.all, by = "ring")
  predictions.ind$logit <- predictions.ind$intercept + predictions.ind$slope * predictions.ind$habitat_val
  predictions.ind$probability <- 1 / (1 + exp(-predictions.ind$logit))  
  
  ## Plot
  
  ### Set colours
  line_colour <- if (grepl("bathy", habitat_var)) {
         bathy_col   } else if (grepl("chl", habitat_var)) {
  chl_col  } else if (grepl("sst", habitat_var)) {
  sst_col } 
  
  pred_plot <- ggplot() +
      geom_line(data = predictions.ind, aes(x = habitat_val, y = probability, group = ID),
                colour = line_colour, alpha = 0.2) +
      facet_grid(~season_type) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(legend.position = "none") +
      labs(y = "Probability of use")
  
  assign(paste0(env_vars[i], "_pred_plot"), pred_plot)
  
}

rnd_effs.out <- do.call("rbind", rnd_effs.list)


## Bathymetry only 

levels_bathy <- levels(pnts_all$dist_shelf_bin)

fixef_vals.between <- fixef(bbal_ker_glmm.between_bathy)$cond
fixef_vals.within <- fixef(bbal_ker_glmm.within_bathy)$cond

# Prepare a data frame to hold predictions
ranef_slopes.between <- ranef(bbal_ker_glmm.between_bathy)$cond$ID
ranef_slopes.within  <- ranef(bbal_ker_glmm.within_bathy)$cond$tripID

pred_df.between <- expand.grid(ID = rownames(ranef_slopes.between),
                       dist_shelf_bin = levels_bathy)
pred_df.within <- expand.grid(ID = rownames(ranef_slopes.within),
                       dist_shelf_bin = levels_bathy)

# Calculate linear predictor per bird & category: - STOPPED HERE
pred_df.between %<>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(rand_int = ranef_slopes.between[ID, "(Intercept)"],
         rand_slope = if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "on_shelf", ranef_slopes.between[ID, "dist_shelf_binon_shelf"],
                      if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "near_break", ranef_slopes.between[ID, "dist_shelf_binnear_break"],
                      ranef_slopes.between[ID, "dist_shelf_binoff_shelf"])),
    fixef_int = fixef_vals.between["(Intercept)"],
    fixef_slope = if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "off_shelf", fixef_vals.between["dist_shelf_binoff_shelf"],
                  if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "near_break", fixef_vals.between["dist_shelf_binnear_break"],
                  0)),
    eta = fixef_int + rand_int + fixef_slope + rand_slope,
    prob = plogis(eta)) %>%
  ungroup()


pred_df.within %<>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(rand_int = ranef_slopes.within[ID, "(Intercept)"],
         rand_slope = if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "on_shelf", ranef_slopes.within[ID, "dist_shelf_binon_shelf"],
                      if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "near_break", ranef_slopes.within[ID, "dist_shelf_binnear_break"],
                      ranef_slopes.within[ID, "dist_shelf_binoff_shelf"])),
    fixef_int = fixef_vals.within["(Intercept)"],
    fixef_slope = if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "off_shelf", fixef_vals.within["dist_shelf_binoff_shelf"],
                  if_else(dist_shelf_bin == "near_break", fixef_vals.within["dist_shelf_binnear_break"],
                  0)),
    eta = fixef_int + rand_int + fixef_slope + rand_slope,
    prob = plogis(eta)) %>%
  ungroup()

## Bind together
pred_df.bathy <- rbind(pred_df.between %>% mutate(season_type = "Between seasons"),
                       pred_df.within %>% mutate(season_type = "Within season"))

# Plot lines connecting points per bird
pred_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = pred_df.bathy, aes(x = dist_shelf_bin, y = prob, group = ID), col = bathy_col, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = pred_df.bathy, aes(x = dist_shelf_bin, y = prob, group = ID), col = bathy_col, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(~season_type) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("On shelf", "Near shelf break", "Off shelf")) +
  labs(x = "Bathymetry category",
       y = "Probability of use") +
  theme_bw()

assign("bathy_pred_plot", pred_plot)

save(rnd_effs.out, file = "Data_outputs/bbal_birdis_habitat_selection.RData")

<!-- #### Habitat preference -->

<!-- After discussion with Sam & Al it was suggested that I could also look at mean habitat use across individuals; essentially I want to look at whether birds are specialists or generalists. Then, the habitat modelling could tell me whether individuals vary in plasticity i.e. are they flexible or specific.  -->

<!-- If I just want to see whether individuals have different preferences, I can do a simple LMM, e.g.:  -->

<!-- $$y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{phase} + \beta_2 \cdot \text{age} + U_{\text{ring}} + U_{\text{season}} + U_{\text{ring:season}} + \varepsilon$$ -->

<!-- where: -->

<!-- -   $y$ represents each of the 3 environmental variables, -->

<!-- -   $\beta_0$ is the intercept, -->

<!-- -   $\beta_1$ - $\beta_{2}$ are fixed effect coefficients for $phase$ and $age$, -->

<!-- -   $U_{\text{ring}}$, $U_{\text{season}}$, and $U_{\text{ring:season}}$ are random intercepts for ring, season, and ring within season respectively, -->

<!--     $$U_{\text{ring}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{ring}})$$ -->

<!--     $$U_{\text{season}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{season}})$$ -->

<!--     $$U_{\text{ring_season}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{ring_season}})$$ -->

<!-- -   $ε$ is the residual error. -->

<!--     $$ε \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{res}})$$ -->

<!-- But if I want to know whether some individuals are more selective than others, I would need to use DHGLMMs. This would allow me to model the variance in selection as a function of individual identity. However, this requires some thought - I tried running a simple DHGLMM, and after 3 days it had only completed 30% of chains. Come back to this. -->

```{r bba_birdis_habitat_preferences, eval = FALSE}

# Integrate meta
load("Data_inputs/ind_meta.RData")
all_ind.meta %<>% filter(species == "BBA") %>% mutate(birthYr = as.numeric(birthYr)) %>% rename(ID = ring)

pnts_all <- merge(pnts_all, all_ind.meta, by = "ID", all.x = T) %>% 
  mutate(ID_season = paste(ID, season, sep = "_"), 
         age = season - birthYr)

pnts_all %<>% filter(!is.na(age))

# Build models

## SST ##
pnts_subset <- pnts_all[sample(nrow(pnts_all), 20000),]

library(brms)

sst_dhglmm <- brm(
  bf(SST ~ phase + age + (1 | ID) + (1 | season)) +
  lf(sigma ~ 0 + ID),
  iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, thin = 10,
  data = pnts_subset)

summary(sst_dhglmm)
save(sst_dhglmm, file = "Data_outputs/test_dhglmm.RData")


sst_pref <- lmer(SST ~ (1 | ID) + (1 | season) + (1 | ID_season) + phase + age,
                 data = pnts_all)

summary(sst_pref)

## Diagnostics
  # plot(m1, resid(., scaled=TRUE) ~ fitted(.), abline = 0)
  # qqnorm(resid(m1))
  # qqline(resid(m1))

```{r waal_birdis_individual, eval = FALSE, fig.cap = "**Figure 2.4.** *Individual level responses to changes in the environmental variables. Individual slopes are plotted for the extent of each individual's range. Black line and grey interval shows population-level response and associated confidence interval.*", fig.topcaption = TRUE}

# Build plots

env_vars = c("sst_scaled", "bathy_scaled", "chl_scaled")

for (i in 1:length(env_vars)) {

  habitat_var = env_vars[i]
  rnd_eff <- get_rnd_effects(mod_between.bbal_bi, habitat_var)
  
  # Get range
  ind_ranges <- pnts_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    summarise(min_sst = min(!!sym(habitat_var), na.rm = TRUE),
              max_sst = max(!!sym(habitat_var), na.rm = TRUE)) 
  
  predictions.ind <- ind_ranges %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(habitat_val = list(seq(min_sst, max_sst, length.out = 100))) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(habitat_val)) 
  
  predictions.ind <- merge(predictions.ind, rnd_eff, by = "ID", all.x = TRUE)
  predictions.ind$logit <- predictions.ind$intercept + predictions.ind$slope * predictions.ind$habitat_val
  predictions.ind$probability <- 1 / (1 + exp(-predictions.ind$logit))  
  
  ## Get global predictions
  predictions.global <- data.frame(ggpredict(mod_between.bbal_bi, terms = paste0(habitat_var, " [all]")))
  
  ## Plot
  pred_plot <- ggplot() +
      geom_line(data = predictions.ind, aes(x = habitat_val, y = probability, colour = abs(slope), group = ID)) +
      scale_colour_gradient(low = "#f4edff", high = "#340088") +  
      geom_line(data = predictions.global, aes(x = x, y = predicted), col = "black",
                 linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
      geom_ribbon(data = predictions.global, aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.5, col = "grey10") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(legend.position = "none") +
      labs(y = "Probability of use")
  
  assign(paste0(env_vars[i], "_pred_plot"), pred_plot)
  
}

```{r waal_birdis_calc_repeatability, eval = FALSE}

# Within season -----
summary(mod_within.waal_bi)

## manual test
vc <- VarCorr(mod_within.waal_bi)

# Variance components 
V_ID_intercept <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[1]^2  
V_ID_sst <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[2]^2        
V_ID_bathy <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[3]^2      
V_ID_chl <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[4]^2        

# Residual variance
V_residual <- (pi^2) / 3  # Residual variance for binary GLMM with logit link

R_sst.within <- V_ID_sst / (V_ID_sst + V_residual)
R_bathy.within <- V_ID_bathy / (V_ID_bathy + V_residual)
R_bathy.within <- V_ID_chl / (V_ID_chl + V_residual)



# Between season -----
summary(mod_between.waal_bi)

## manual test
vc <- VarCorr(mod_between.waal_bi)

# Variance components 
V_ID_intercept <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[1]^2  
V_ID_sst <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[2]^2

# APPENDICES

At this point I have (1) randomly sampled available habitat on a ratio
of 6 available to 1 used points; and (2) matched up all of these points
with environmental data - specifically, SST, bathymetry, SSH, and
chlorophyll.

To ensure appropriate model fit, I'll be working on each species/colony
separately. I can think about integrating them later, if the residual
distributions etc are similar.

Apart from this, the correlations don't seem very worrying. In response
to these correlations, I dropped SSH.

#### Average preference

Here I'm looking at differences in average habitat choice amongst
individuals. Here, I fit simple linear models where the average
environmental variable experienced is predicted by distance from the
colony, breeding phase, and - critically - the random effect of
individual.

From this I can extract random intercepts as the variation in
environment use attributable to individual - e.g. average value of SST
for each individual - and then the repeatability of individual choice
for the environmental variable.

The model I fitted was:

$$y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{dist_col} + \beta_2 \cdot \text{phase} + U_{\text{ID}} + U_{\text{tripID}}$$

where:

-   $\beta_0$ is the intercept,
-   $\beta_1$ is the fixed effect of the distance from the colony (to
    control for environmental variation associated with this),
-   $\beta_2$ is the fixed effects of breeding phase,
-   $U_{\text{ID}}$ is the individual-level random intercept,
-   $U_{\text{ID}}$ is the random intercept for trip.

```{r average_habitat}

pnts.used <- pnts_all %>% filter(used == 1)

env_vars <- c("SST", "bathy", "chl")
rpt_df <- data.frame(env_var = character(), rpt_R = numeric())

for (i in 1:length(env_vars)) {
  
  # Fit the linear mixed model
  mod <- lmer(as.formula(paste(env_vars[i], "~ dist_col + phase + (1 | ID) + (1 | tripID)")), data = pnts.used)
  
  # Extract random effects for ID
  random_effects <- ranef(mod)$ID
  ind_intercepts <- random_effects[, 1]
  
  # Extract fixed effects for the intercept
  ind_avg <- ind_intercepts + fixef(mod)[1]
  assign(paste0("ind_avg.", env_vars[i]), ind_avg)
  
  # Calculate variance components
  var_components <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod))
  var_id <- var_components[var_components$grp == "ID", "vcov"]
  var_residual <- attr(VarCorr(mod), "sc")^2
  
  # Total variance = variance from ID + residual variance
  total_var <- var_id + var_residual
  
  # Calculate repeatability
  repeatability <- var_id / total_var
  
  # Output
  rpt_df <- rbind(rpt_df, data.frame(variable = env_vars[i], repeatability = repeatability))
 
}

## Plot outputs
ind_avg.plot <- data.frame(SST = ind_avg.sst,
                           bathy = ind_avg.bathy,
                           chl = ind_avg.chl)

ind_avg_long <- ind_avg.plot %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  arrange(variable) %>%
  mutate(dummy_x = 1)

# Add y position for plot: SST - bathy - chl
rpt_df$y_position = c(8, 1200, 4)

ind_avg_long_with_rpt <- ind_avg_long %>%
  left_join(rpt_df, by = "variable")

# Plot
label_map <- c(
  bathy = "Bathymetry (m below sea level)",
  chl = "Chlorophyll (mg Chl m^-3)",
  SST = "SST (°C)")

png(filename = "Figures/avg_environment.png", width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", res = 600)
ggplot(ind_avg_long_with_rpt, aes(x = dummy_x, y = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, colour = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
   # Add the repeatability text
  geom_text(aes(x = 1, y = y_position, label = paste("Repeatability: ", round(repeatability, 3))),
            fontface = "plain", colour = "black", size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y", 
             labeller = labeller(variable = label_map)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#37D5AC", "#339F48", "#A0307E")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank())
dev.off()



```

#### Habitat selection models

To understand individual variation in habitat preference, I am fitting
habitat selection models. These are binomial models that look at
differences in environmental conditions between 'used' and 'available'
habitats. I have fitted a random slope to allow indiviudal selection to
vary.

After having issues fitting each environmental variable in turn
(specifically, the AUC was very low, suggesting poor predictive
performance), I realised that a maximal model including all the
predictors might be better. Indeed, I get better AUC and fit (see
below).

This current model is only looking at between season individual
variation, I still need to look at within season.

The generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) used in this analysis is:

$$\text{logit}(\Pr(\text{used} = 1)) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{sst} + \beta_2 \cdot \text{sst}^2 + \beta_3 \cdot \text{bathy} + \beta_4 \cdot \text{bathy}^2 + \beta_5 \cdot \text{chl} + \beta_6 \cdot \text{dist col} + \beta_7 \cdot \text{phase} + U_{\text{ID}} + U_{\text{ID}}^{\text{sst}} \cdot \text{sst} + U_{\text{ID}}^{\text{bathy}} \cdot \text{bathy} + U_{\text{ID}}^{\text{chl}} \cdot \text{chl}$$

where:

-   $\beta_0$ is the intercept,
-   $\beta_1$–$\beta_{7}$ are the fixed effects of each environmental
    variable ($sst$, $bathy$, $chl$), breeding phase ($phase$), and
    distance from the colony in km ($dist col$)
-   $U_{\text{ID}}$ is the individual-level random intercept,
-   $U_{\text{ID}}^{\text{sst}}$, $U_{\text{ID}}^{\text{bathy}}$, and
-   $U_{\text{ID}}^{\text{chl}}$ are **individual-level random slopes**
    for **SST, bathymetry, and chlorophyll**, allowing individuals to
    have **different responses** to these variables.

Both SST and bathymetry were fitted with quadratic effects based on
exploratory modelling. For SST, it looks like birds select medium-low
temperatures; for bathymetry it looks like birds prefer shallow and deep
areas (possibly confounded by colony distance, but we'll get on to
that). Models fitted with quadratic SST and bathymetry are a
significiantly better fit based on AIC and an ANOVA comparison. The
binned residual plot also looks considerably better, and the AUC
improves (marginally, as it was reasonably good to begin with). Most
importantly, I have no convergence issues with this model structure.

I have not included quadratic random slopes as this gets very
complicated. So for now, we are assuming that all birds have the same
quadratic preference (same slope shape) but this can 'shift'.

```{r plot_individual_slopes}

env_variables <- c("sst", "bathy", "chl")
env_colours <- c(
  "sst" = "#A0307E",
  "bathy" = "#37D5AC",
  "chl" = "#339F48")

env_labels <- c(
  "sst" = "Scaled SST",
  "bathy" = "Scaled bathymetry",
  "chl" = "Scaled chlorophyll conc.")

rpt_list <- list() 
within = TRUE

for (i in seq_along(env_variables)) {
  
  if (within == TRUE) {
    mod_loaded <-loadRData(paste0("Data_outputs/mod_brms_quad_", env_variables[i], "_within.RData")) } else {
      mod_loaded <-loadRData(paste0("Data_outputs/mod_brms_quad_", env_variables[i], ".RData"))
    }
  
  env_scaled <- paste0(env_variables[i], "_scaled")
  
  # Get variances
  posterior <- as_draws_df(mod_loaded)
  var_col <- ifelse(within == TRUE, paste0("sd_ID_season__", env_scaled), paste0("sd_ID__", env_scaled))
  var_among <- posterior[[var_col]]^2 
  var_resid <- pi^2 / 3
  
  # Calculate repeatability per posterior sample
  repeatability <- var_among / (var_among + var_resid)
  repeatability_summary <- data.frame(
    var = env_variables[i],
    mean = mean(repeatability),
    median = median(repeatability),
    CI_lower = quantile(repeatability, 0.025),
    CI_upper = quantile(repeatability, 0.975))
  
  rpt_list[[i]] <- repeatability_summary
  
  # Extract random & fixed effects
  re <- ranef(mod_loaded)[[1]]
  fixed <- fixef(mod_loaded)
  
  # Build data frame of individual slopes
  slopes <- data.frame(
    ID = rownames(re),
    intercept = fixed["Intercept", "Estimate"] + re[, "Estimate", "Intercept"],
    slope = fixed[env_scaled, "Estimate"] + re[, "Estimate", env_scaled])
  
  if(env_variables[i] == "chl") {
    slopes$quad = NA
  } else {
    slopes$quad = fixed[paste0(env_scaled, 2), "Estimate"] + re[, "Estimate", paste0(env_scaled, 2)] 
  }
  
   
  png(file = ifelse(within == TRUE, 
                    paste0("Figures/individual_", env_variables[i], "_within_slopes.png"), 
                    paste0("Figures/individual_", env_variables[i], "_between_slopes.png")),
                    width = 5, height = 4, units = "in", res = 600)
  ggplot(slopes, aes(x = reorder(ID, slope), y = slope)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = fixed[env_scaled, "Estimate"], linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(y = "Individual slope", x = "Individual ID") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) 
  dev.off()
  
  png(file =ifelse(within == TRUE, 
                    paste0("Figures/histogram_", env_variables[i], "_within_slopes.png"), 
                    paste0("Figures/histogram_", env_variables[i], "_between_slopes.png")),
      width = 5, height = 4, units = "in", res = 600)
  ggplot(slopes, aes(x = slope)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    labs(x = "Individual slope", y = "Count") +
    theme_bw() 
  dev.off()
  
  # Plot individual curves
  ## Create a sequence of environmental variables
  env_seq <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100)
  
  # Expand to a grid: one row per individual per sst_scaled value
  curve_data <- slopes %>%
    mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
    slice(rep(1:n(), each = length(env_seq))) %>%
    mutate(env_scaled = rep(env_seq, times = nrow(slopes)),
           env_scaled2 = env_scaled^2)
  
  if(env_variables[i] == "chl") {
    curve_data %<>%
      mutate(logit_p = intercept + slope * env_scaled,
             prob = plogis(logit_p))
  } else {
    curve_data %<>%
      mutate(logit_p = intercept + slope * env_scaled + quad * env_scaled2,
             prob = plogis(logit_p))
  }

  colour_choice <- env_colours[env_variables[i]]
  x_label <- env_labels[env_variables[i]]
  
  png(file = ifelse(within == TRUE, 
                    paste0("Figures/individual_", env_variables[i], "_within_curves.png"), 
                    paste0("Figures/individual_", env_variables[i], "_between_curves.png")), 
      width = 6.5, height = 6, units = "in", res = 600)
  ggplot(curve_data, aes(x = env_scaled, y = prob, group = ID)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.3, colour = colour_choice) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = "P|used") +
    theme_bw()
  dev.off()

}


```

```{r code from Bertille}

load("Data_outputs/mod_brms.quad.Rdata")
summary(mod_brms.quad)

set.seed(817)
pnts_subset <- pnts_all[sample(nrow(pnts_all), 50000),]

# Onset of senescence
df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$OnsetSenescence = - df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$Slope / (2*df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$Slope2 )


# extract rate of senescence
# Function that calculates the derivative of 
# exp(quad*xval^2+lin*xval+const)/(1+exp(quad*xval^2+lin*xval+const))
deriv_logit_quad<-function(xval,quad,lin,const)
{
  output<-(2*quad*xval+lin)*exp(quad*xval^2+lin*xval+const)/((1+exp(quad*xval^2+lin*xval+const))^2)
  return(output)
}
 
# Find minimum of the derivative 
xinfl<-c()
gradmins<-c()
for(index in 1:length(df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$Slope2))
{
  minval<-optimize(deriv_logit_quad,c(0,100),df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$Slope2[index],df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$Slope[index],df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$Intercept[index]) 
  xinfl<-c(xinfl,minval$minimum)
  gradmins<-c(gradmins,minval$objective)
}
 
# Add to df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevelframe and put out to CSV
df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$SenesceRate<-gradmins
df_rawAge_randomSlopesAndInterceptsIDlevel$ageInfl<-xinfl

# Check for correlations

# Check for patterns and that most points are within 95% confidence intervals
plot_binnedplot(mod_between.bbal_bi)

# Check ratio is close to 1
overdisp.mod <- overdisp_fun(mod_between.bbal_bi)

# Check ratio: >1 may indicate zero inflation (more 0s than expected); < 1 zero deflation
# Small P = evidence to suggest zero-inflation/deflation
zeroinf.mod <- testZeroInflation(mod_between.bbal_bi, plot = FALSE)

```

#### Model diagnostics

-   In the most simple model, season explained essentially no variation,
    so I dropped this.
-   The AUC value was \> 0.5, which suggests the model separates 'used'
    vs. 'not used' locations very well, or in other words, the
    predictors are strongly informative.
-   The VIF values are all \< 2, so there is no concerning
    multicollinearity.
-   The overdispersion function is slightly high. This could indicate
    moderate overdispersion (i.e. variance is higher than expected in a
    binomial model), but probably not a major concern.
-   There is some evidence for zero-inflation. However, this might be to
    expected, as zero counts are an inherent part of the process I am
    trying to model, and so a zero-inflated approach is likely
    unnecessary.

I am getting some convergence warnings, which, coupled with the high
variance in my slopes, might suggest that the random effects can't be
trusted. This could be because I have too many complex random effects,
or sparse data per group. I should probably try to fit the random
effects separately...

The results show that in general, birds select for median SST, deeper
waters, higher chlorophyll concentrations, and locations closer to the
colony. There is a high degree of individual variation, especially in
the use of SST and bathymetry.

#### Individual effects

```{r bbal_birdis_individual_within, fig.cap = "**Figure 1.4.** *Within-season, individual level responses to changes in the environmental variables. Individual slopes are plotted for the extent of each individual's range. Black line and grey interval shows population-level response and associated confidence interval.*", fig.topcaption = TRUE}

# Build plots
load("Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_within_sst.RData")

env_vars = c("sst_scaled", "bathy_scaled", "chl_scaled")

for (i in 1:length(env_vars)) {

  habitat_var = env_vars[i]
  rnd_eff <- get_rnd_effects(mod_within.bbal_bi, habitat_var)
  
  # Get range
  ind_ranges <- pnts_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    summarise(min_sst = min(!!sym(habitat_var), na.rm = TRUE),
              max_sst = max(!!sym(habitat_var), na.rm = TRUE)) 
  
  predictions.ind <- ind_ranges %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(habitat_val = list(seq(min_sst, max_sst, length.out = 100))) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(habitat_val)) 
  
  predictions.ind <- merge(predictions.ind, rnd_eff, by = "ID", all.x = TRUE)
  predictions.ind$logit <- predictions.ind$intercept + predictions.ind$slope * predictions.ind$habitat_val
  predictions.ind$probability <- 1 / (1 + exp(-predictions.ind$logit))  
  
  ## Get global predictions
  predictions.global <- data.frame(ggpredict(mod_within.bbal_bi, terms = paste0(habitat_var, " [all]")))
  
  ## Plot
  pred_plot <- ggplot() +
      geom_line(data = predictions.ind, aes(x = habitat_val, y = probability, colour = abs(slope), group = ID)) +
      scale_colour_gradient(low = "#f4edff", high = "#340088") +  
      geom_line(data = predictions.global, aes(x = x, y = predicted), col = "black",
                 linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
      geom_ribbon(data = predictions.global, aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.5, col = "grey10") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(legend.position = "none") +
      labs(y = "Probability of use")
  
  assign(paste0(env_vars[i], "_pred_plot"), pred_plot)
  
}

```{r bbal_birdis_calc_repeatability}

# Within season -----
summary(mod_within.bbal_bi)

## manual test
vc <- VarCorr(mod_within.bbal_bi)

# Variance components 
V_ID_intercept <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[1]^2  
V_ID_sst <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[2]^2        
V_ID_bathy <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[3]^2      
V_ID_chl <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[4]^2        

# Residual variance
V_residual <- (pi^2) / 3  # Residual variance for binary GLMM with logit link

R_sst.within <- V_ID_sst / (V_ID_sst + V_residual)
R_bathy.within <- V_ID_bathy / (V_ID_bathy + V_residual)
R_bathy.within <- V_ID_chl / (V_ID_chl + V_residual)



# Between season -----
summary(mod_between.bbal_bi)

## manual test
vc <- VarCorr(mod_between.bbal_bi)

# Variance components 
V_ID_intercept <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[1]^2  
V_ID_sst <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[2]^2        
V_ID_bathy <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[3]^2      
V_ID_chl <- attr(vc$ID, "stddev")[4]^2        

# Residual variance
V_residual <- (pi^2) / 3  # Residual variance for binary GLMM with logit link

R_sst.between <- V_ID_sst / (V_ID_sst + V_residual)
R_bathy.between <- V_ID_bathy / (V_ID_bathy + V_residual)
R_bathy.between <- V_ID_chl / (V_ID_chl + V_residual)

# Understanding within-individual centering

Currently, the model is fitted with within-population centering of the
environmental variables - i.e., each variable has been scaled to the
mean and 2SD of the entire datasets. Conversely, within-individual
centering removes between-individual variation, allowing me to focus
just on within-individual responses (i.e. plasticity).

Here I am trying a few different model structures to better understand
how within-individual centering, random slopes, and quadratic random
slopes change the predictions of my models. For simplicity, I have
removed the distance effect and the phase effect.

```{r exploring_structures, eval = FALSE}

#set.seed(817)
#pnts_subset <- pnts_all[sample(nrow(pnts_all), 50000),]

#pnts_subset <- pnts_all

# Population centering, linear slope ----

mod_pop_linear <- glmmTMB(
  used ~ sst_scaled + sst_scaled2 + poly(bathy_scaled, 2) + chl_scaled +
         (1 + sst_scaled | ID_season) + (1 | tripID),
  data = pnts_subset,
  family = binomial()
)

summary(mod_pop_linear)
save(mod_pop_linear, file = "Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_pop_linear.RData")

# Population centering, quadratic slope ----

mod_pop_quad <- glmmTMB(
  used ~ sst_scaled + sst_scaled2 + poly(bathy_scaled, 2) + chl_scaled + dist_col_scaled + phase +
         (sst_scaled + sst_scaled2 | ID_season) + (1 | tripID),
  data = pnts_subset,
  family = binomial()
)

summary(mod_pop_quad)
save(mod_pop_quad, file = "Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_pop_quad.RData")


# Within-individual centering, linear slope ----

mod_ind_linear <- glmmTMB(
  used ~ sst_within + sst_within2 + poly(bathy_scaled, 2) + chl_scaled + dist_col_scaled + phase +
         (1 + sst_within | ID_season) + (1 | tripID),
  data = pnts_subset,
  family = binomial()
)

save(mod_ind_linear, file = "Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_ind_linear.RData")

# Within-individual centering, quadratic slope ----

mod_ind_quad <- glmmTMB(
  used ~ sst_within + sst_within2 + poly(bathy_scaled, 2) + chl_scaled + dist_col_scaled + phase +
         (sst_within + sst_within2 | ID_season) + (1 | tripID),
  data = pnts_subset,
  family = binomial()
)

save(mod_ind_quad, file = "Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_ind_quad.RData")

```{r exploring_structures_plots, eval = TRUE}

load("Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_pop_linear.RData")
load("Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_pop_quad.RData")
load("Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_ind_linear.RData")
load("Data_outputs/bba_birdis_habitat_model_ind_quad.RData")

# set.seed(817)
# pnts_subset <- pnts_all[sample(nrow(pnts_all), 50000),]

# Get individual range
ind_ranges <- pnts_subset %>%
    mutate(ID_season = paste(ring, season, sep = "_")) %>%
    group_by(ID_season) %>%
    summarise(min_sst = min(sst_scaled, na.rm = TRUE),
              max_sst = max(sst_scaled, na.rm = TRUE)) 

predictions.ind <- ind_ranges %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(sst_scaled = list(seq(min_sst, max_sst, length.out = 100))) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(sst_scaled)) %>%
    mutate(sst_scaled2 = sst_scaled^2)

predictions.ind_within <- pnts_subset %>% group_by(ID_season) %>% select(ID_season, sst_within, sst_within2)

# Population centering, linear slope ----
rnd_eff <- ranef(mod_pop_linear)
rnd_eff <- rnd_eff$cond$ID_season
rnd_eff$ID_season <- rownames(rnd_eff)
rownames(rnd_eff) <- NULL
rnd_eff %<>% rename(slope = sst_scaled, intercept = '(Intercept)')

predictions.ind_pop.linear <- merge(predictions.ind, rnd_eff, by = "ID_season", all.x = TRUE)
predictions.ind_pop.linear$logit <- predictions.ind_pop.linear$intercept + predictions.ind_pop.linear$slope * predictions.ind_pop.linear$sst_scaled
predictions.ind_pop.linear$probability <- 1 / (1 + exp(-predictions.ind_pop.linear$logit))  
  
## Plot
predictions.ind_pop.linear %<>% separate(ID_season, into = c("ring", "season"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>% mutate(ring_num = as.numeric(as.factor(ring)))

plot_pop.linear <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = predictions.ind_pop.linear, aes(x = sst_scaled, y = probability, colour = ring_num, group = ID_season), alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#f4edff", high = "#340088") +  
      theme_bw() +
      theme(legend.position = "none") +
      labs(y = "Probability of use", x = "SST, scaled", title = "Linear random slope, population-level environmental centering")


# Population centering, quadratic slope ----

rnd_eff_pop_quad <- ranef(mod_pop_quad)
rnd_eff_pop_quad <- rnd_eff_pop_quad$cond$ID_season
rnd_eff_pop_quad$ID_season <- rownames(rnd_eff_pop_quad)
rownames(rnd_eff_pop_quad) <- NULL
rnd_eff_pop_quad %<>% rename(slope_linear = sst_scaled, slope_quadratic = sst_scaled2, intercept = '(Intercept)')

predictions.ind_pop.quad <- merge(predictions.ind, rnd_eff_pop_quad, by = "ID_season", all.x = TRUE)
predictions.ind_pop.quad$logit <- predictions.ind_pop.quad$intercept + 
                                  predictions.ind_pop.quad$slope_linear * predictions.ind_pop.quad$sst_scaled + 
                                  predictions.ind_pop.quad$slope_quadratic * predictions.ind_pop.quad$sst_scaled2
predictions.ind_pop.quad$probability <- 1 / (1 + exp(-predictions.ind_pop.quad$logit))

## Plot
predictions.ind_pop.quad %<>% separate(ID_season, into = c("ring", "season"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>% mutate(ring_num = as.numeric(as.factor(ring)))

    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(y = "Probability of use", x = "SST, scaled", title = "Quadratic random slope, population-level environmental centering")
